week.weeklyOverview: Communication starts long before first words. This week focuses on warm, face-to-face turn-taking with infants (about 0–6 months) through mirrors, soft puppets, family photos, and responsive cooing games. Teachers pause after each greeting so babies can answer with eyes, smiles, kicks, or sounds. Experiences stay short and relationship-centered—no crafts, no finished products, just meaningful back-and-forth.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Baby-safe unbreakable mirrors
Laminated family photo cards
Soft hand puppets
Small soft plush faces
Simple face picture cards
Sturdy board books with faces
Lightweight scarves for peek games
Gentle musical toys (soft volume)
Floor mats / nursing pillows for supported sitting
Optional voice-recording buttons with caregiver voices (secure cases)
Name tags with large print for caregivers
week.teacherPreparation: Stage soft materials at floor level before arrival. Follow infant cues; keep Baby's First Conversations invitations short and responsive.
week.familyConnection: Talk with your baby throughout daily routines—diapering, feeding, walks. Say one short sentence, then pause and watch for a blink, coo, or wiggle. Copy their sounds sometimes, then add a gentle new word. These tiny conversations build trust and early language even before words appear.
milestones: Language: Coos, vocalizes, or mouth-moves in response to a caregiver’s greeting and pausing
SEL: Shares social smiles and sustained face-looking with a trusted adult
Motor: Turns head toward voices, tracks faces briefly, and activates arms/legs during playful talk
Cognition: Notices familiar faces in mirrors/photos and anticipates peek or turn-taking games

printableIdeas.title: Hello Face Picture Card Pack
printableIdeas.purpose: Large smile/look/listen cards support Face-to-Face Chat Time and puppet greetings without cluttering the infant’s visual field.

printableIdeas.title: Family Photo Conversation Frames
printableIdeas.purpose: Simple frame templates help teachers mount family photos securely for photo chat albums and goodbye rituals.

songs.title: Hello Little Friend
songs.motions: Gentle wave near midline; point softly toward baby’s eyes; place hand on your heart on wait; open palms inviting a response.
songs.teacherDirections: Sing face-to-face at baby’s eye level. After answer right, pause 3–5 seconds for any response, then mirror the baby’s sound or smile. Keep to one or two verses.
songs.whenToUse: Morning greeting, Hello Song Circle, or one-to-one arrival welcome
songs.transitionPurpose: Signal connection time and practice conversational pausing
songs.lyrics:
Hello, hello, little friend,
I see your eyes—let’s talk again.
Hello, hello, smile so bright,
I wait for you to answer right.

songs.title: Coo With Me
songs.motions: Exaggerate calm mouth shapes; lean in slightly on wait; soft sway; clap once gently at the end if baby enjoys sound.
songs.teacherDirections: Use during Coo Back Conversation. Model one sound, pause, then respond to whatever baby offers—including silence with a warm smile.
songs.whenToUse: Floor play vocal games and mid-morning connection resets
songs.transitionPurpose: Prime listening/turn-taking before puppet or photo chats
songs.lyrics:
Coo with me, coo with you,
I say ‘ah,’ then wait for you.
Babble soft, babble near,
Your little voice is music here.

songs.title: The More We Get Together
songs.motions: Soft side-to-side rock while holding baby securely; gentle wave on friends; smile connection at the close.
songs.teacherDirections: Use with supported hold or tummy-to-tummy. Keep volume soft. Invite a second caregiver to join for social warmth without crowding the infant’s face.
songs.whenToUse: Small-group closing or family photo conversation wind-down
songs.transitionPurpose: Celebrate belonging and close the conversation circle
songs.lyrics:
The more we get together, together, together,
The more we get together, the happier we’ll be.
For your friends are my friends, and my friends are your friends.
The more we get together, the happier we’ll be.

books.whyThisBook: Rhythmic greetings and animal faces invite infants to look, listen, and enjoy social hello language.
beforeReadingQuestions: Shall we say hello to the baby on the cover?
duringReadingPrompts: Hello, little one—can you look at this face with me?
afterReadingQuestions: Let’s say hello one more time to you!
books.substituteTitle: Use Hello Little Friend chant with a soft puppet if the book is unavailable.

teacherToolkit.teacherPreparation: Stage soft materials at floor level before arrival. Follow infant cues; keep Baby's First Conversations invitations short and responsive.
prepChecklist: Set materials at child height before arrival
Preview one Baby's First Conversations invitation aloud
Place cleanup caddy near the play space
Review allergy and supervision notes for the day
observationFocus: Uses Baby's First Conversations vocabulary in play
Persists with a material or peer exchange
Shows interest or curiosity during invitations
observationPrompts: What language or gestures appear during play?
How does the child enter and leave the invitation?
Where do peers support or extend the idea?
documentationPrompts: Capture one moment of child-led exploration (with permission).
Note a verbatim quote or gesture tied to the theme.
teacherTips: Model once, then narrate what you notice.
Offer two choices instead of open-ended demands.
Keep transitions short with a familiar song cue.
setupCleanupShortcuts: Trays labeled and stacked by day
Damp cloth + bin for quick reset
Spare substitution basket on the shelf

materialSubstitutions.use: printed picture cards or recycled clean containers

teacherToolkit.mixedAgeAdaptations: Pair floor play with a nearby toddler shelf; older peers model gentle touch only with adult nearby.
teacherToolkit.extraSupportAdaptations: Sit beside, shorten the invitation, and offer hand-under-hand only when welcomed.
teacherToolkit.challengeExtensions: Invite children to invent a new Baby's First Conversations rule, map, or story for peers.
teacherToolkit.safetyInclusionNotes: For young infants, prioritize supervised floor or supported holds—never prop bottles or leave babies unattended on elevated surfaces. Mirrors must be unbreakable and secured. Scarves are for brief peek games only (no wrapping). Avoid small parts and finished-product crafts. Reduce noise and visual clutter so faces stay the main focus. Always follow cue-based caregiving: pause, watch, then respond.
teacherToolkit.endOfWeekReflection: Which Baby's First Conversations words and strategies showed up most in play?
teacherToolkit.familyConnection: Share one Baby's First Conversations word or song to try at home during ordinary routines.
teacherToolkit.notes: Draft toolkit for owner review — enrichment draft only.

legacySnapshot.weeklyOverview: Communication begins long before babies say their first words. Throughout this week, infants will engage in meaningful back-and-forth interactions through facial expressions, coos, babbles, songs, mirrors, gestures, and responsive caregiving. These experiences help build the foundation for language development, social connection, listening skills, and emotional security.
legacySnapshot.objectives:
- Encourage early communication skills
- Support cooing, babbling, and vocal play
- Strengthen caregiver-child interactions
- Develop listening and turn-taking skills
- Promote facial recognition and social engagement
- Build early language foundations
